exercises.title: One index for filter + sort: the composite index
exercises.problemHtml:
The profile page shows a user's 5 latest events: SELECT * FROM event WHERE user_id = 42 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 5. Create ONE index that lets PostgreSQL find user 42's rows already sorted by time, so the plan has no Sort node.

Sample tables (chapters 9–10)

event (id identity PK, user_id int, status text, amount numeric(10,2), email text, created_at timestamptz, props jsonb)
      20 000 rows: user_id 1–2000 (10 events each) · status pending 1 %, done ~33 %, active ~66 %
      email 'user<g>@example.com' (unique) · created_at every 10 minutes from 2024-01-01 · props {"plan": "free"|"pro", "device": …}
users (id PK, name, country)   2 000 rows
No index except the primary keys. Statistics are collected (ANALYZE) so the planner behaves like on a real server.
Helpers: plan_nodes(q) / plan_text(q) / plan_rows(q) / plan_analyze(q) print the plan of query text q.

The lesson used 500 000 rows; 20 000 deterministic rows are enough for the planner to make the same choices. The grader is PostgreSQL 18 (WASM).

Requirements

  • A composite index: the equality column first, then the sort column.
  • The plan must contain Index Cond: (user_id = 42) and no Sort.

Bài giảng dùng 500 000 dòng; 20 000 dòng tất định đủ để bộ lập kế hoạch chọn giống vậy. Máy chấm là PostgreSQL 18 (WASM).

Yêu cầu

  • Chỉ mục tổ hợp: cột so bằng trước, cột sắp xếp sau.
  • Kế hoạch phải có Index Cond: (user_id = 42) và không có Sort.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: In (user_id, created_at) all entries of user 42 are contiguous and already ordered by created_at, so PostgreSQL reads 5 entries backwards and stops — no sort, no extra rows. Column order decides which queries an index can serve.
exercises.solutionExplanationHtmlVi: Trong (user_id, created_at) mọi mục của user 42 nằm liền nhau và đã sắp theo created_at, nên PostgreSQL đọc ngược 5 mục rồi dừng — không sắp, không dòng thừa. Thứ tự cột quyết định chỉ mục phục vụ được truy vấn nào.

exercises.title: A covering index: Index Only Scan
exercises.problemHtml:
The wallet widget runs SELECT user_id, sum(amount) FROM event WHERE user_id = 42 GROUP BY user_id. Create an index on user_id that also carries amount, so the query can be answered from the index alone (Index Only Scan) without visiting the table.

Sample tables (chapters 9–10)

event (id identity PK, user_id int, status text, amount numeric(10,2), email text, created_at timestamptz, props jsonb)
      20 000 rows: user_id 1–2000 (10 events each) · status pending 1 %, done ~33 %, active ~66 %
      email 'user<g>@example.com' (unique) · created_at every 10 minutes from 2024-01-01 · props {"plan": "free"|"pro", "device": …}
users (id PK, name, country)   2 000 rows
No index except the primary keys. Statistics are collected (ANALYZE) so the planner behaves like on a real server.
Helpers: plan_nodes(q) / plan_text(q) / plan_rows(q) / plan_analyze(q) print the plan of query text q.

The lesson used 500 000 rows; 20 000 deterministic rows are enough for the planner to make the same choices. The grader is PostgreSQL 18 (WASM).

Requirements

  • CREATE INDEX … ON event (user_id) INCLUDE (amount).
  • The check turns off bitmap scans so you can see the node the index enables.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: A covering index contains every column of the query, so PostgreSQL can skip the table. On a real server, how often it really skips depends on the visibility map (VACUUM) — EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows it as "Heap Fetches".

exercises.title: Index the foreign key you join and sort on (CT Shop)
concepts: FK columns are not indexed automatically
exercises.problemHtml:
Two hot queries of CT Shop: (1) "my orders, newest first": SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 3 ORDER BY created_at DESC; (2) "who bought this product": SELECT order_id FROM order_item WHERE product_id = 31. Neither foreign-key column has an index. Create exactly the two indexes that serve them (no Sort for the first one).

Sample database: CT Shop mini (the course's lab project, sliced)

customer       (id PK, email UNIQUE lower-case, full_name, phone NULL, city DEFAULT 'Hà Nội', created_at timestamptz)
category       (id PK, name UNIQUE, parent_id → category.id — NULL = root)       12 rows: 1–4 roots, 5–12 children
product        (id PK, sku UNIQUE, name, category_id → category, price numeric(12,2) > 0, stock int ≥ 0 DEFAULT 0,
                attrs jsonb DEFAULT '{}', is_active boolean DEFAULT true, created_at)          16 rows (ids 1…46, gaps)
orders         (id PK, customer_id → customer, status pending|paid|shipped|cancelled, created_at timestamptz, note)   14 rows
order_item     (order_id → orders ON DELETE CASCADE, product_id → product, qty > 0, unit_price) — PK (order_id, product_id)
payment        (id PK, order_id UNIQUE → orders, amount, method cod|card|momo|bank, paid_at)    one per paid/shipped order
stock_movement (id PK, product_id → product, change ≠ 0, reason import|sale|return|adjust, order_id NULL, created_at)
review         (id PK, product_id → product, customer_id → customer, rating 1–5, body, created_at) — UNIQUE (product_id, customer_id)

Same 8 tables as Labs 1–9 (in schema public instead of shop); the rows are a small slice of the lab data — same category tree, same product ids/SKUs/prices. Every id is GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY: leave it out of INSERT. Times are timestamptz shown in Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh. Full script: the ctshop.sql tab.

Plus the plan helper functions (plan_text …). The table is tiny, so the checks switch sequential scans off to ask "COULD an index serve this?".

Requirements

  • orders (customer_id, created_at) (DESC optional — B-trees scan both ways).
  • order_item (product_id) — the PK (order_id, product_id) starts with order_id, so it does not help.

  name       text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  parent_id  int  REFERENCES category(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
);

  id           bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  sku          text          NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name         text          NOT NULL,
  category_id  int           NOT NULL REFERENCES category(id),
  price        numeric(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (price > 0),
  stock        int           NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (stock >= 0),
  attrs        jsonb         NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  is_active    boolean       NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  created_at   timestamptz   NOT NULL DEFAULT now()

CREATE FUNCTION plan_nodes(q text) RETURNS text LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $f$
DECLARE j json; out text := '';
BEGIN
  EXECUTE 'EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON, COSTS OFF) ' || q INTO j;
  WITH RECURSIVE n(p) AS (SELECT j -> 0 -> 'Plan' UNION ALL SELECT x FROM n, json_array_elements(n.p -> 'Plans') x)
  SELECT string_agg((p ->> 'Node Type') || coalesce(' on ' || (p ->> 'Index Name'), ''), ' / ') INTO out FROM n;
  RETURN out;
END $f$;
CREATE FUNCTION plan_text(q text) RETURNS text LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $f$
DECLARE r record; out text := '';
BEGIN
  FOR r IN EXECUTE 'EXPLAIN (COSTS OFF) ' || q LOOP out := out || r."QUERY PLAN" || E'\n'; END LOOP;
  RETURN out;
END $f$;
CREATE FUNCTION plan_rows(q text) RETURNS bigint LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $f$
DECLARE j json;
BEGIN
  EXECUTE 'EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) ' || q INTO j;
  RETURN (j -> 0 -> 'Plan' ->> 'Plan Rows')::numeric::bigint;
END $f$;
CREATE FUNCTION plan_analyze(q text) RETURNS text LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $f$
DECLARE r record; out text := '';
BEGIN
  FOR r IN EXECUTE 'EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, COSTS OFF, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF, BUFFERS OFF) ' || q LOOP out := out || r."QUERY PLAN" || E'\n'; END LOOP;
  RETURN out;
END $f$;

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: Missing indexes on foreign keys are the most common production slowdown (chapter 16): every "children of X" query and every DELETE of a parent scans the child table. On a tiny table the planner prefers a seq scan anyway — turning enable_seqscan off in the check asks whether an index could serve the query at all.
exercises.solutionExplanationHtmlVi: Thiếu chỉ mục trên khoá ngoại là nguyên nhân chậm phổ biến nhất trên production (chương 16): mọi truy vấn "con của X" và mọi lệnh DELETE cha đều quét bảng con. Trên bảng nhỏ, planner vẫn thích quét tuần tự — tắt enable_seqscan trong kiểm là hỏi chỉ mục có thể phục vụ truy vấn hay không.

  parent_id  int  REFERENCES category(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
